limits: Edges with unchecked access rules are not routable by default. That removes 465 of 5661 edges, or 27.6 km.
The largest routable network holds 81.5% of routable nodes and 87.5% of routable length.
Kerbs do not trigger an access check. 2 edges that cross a raised kerb carry the steps flag, so step-free routes avoid them.
Gates alone remove 389 edges and 22.0 km. Village and estate gates need a field check.
Only access, foot and opening-hours rules restrict walkers. Vehicle-only conditional tags, such as a Sunday car-free rule, do not.
Indoor corridors and building passages without cited hours stay unroutable. They remove 1 edges and 0.0 km.
The graph leaves out 458 whole ways, 6.7 km, that touch an explicitly closed node.
2 indoor edges with cited mall hours are routable. The router opens and closes them by those hours.
The routable graph has 1.51 km of roofed, tunnel or indoor walkway in 70 edges.
OSM maps 5 indoor, corridor or passage edges here. 3 of them carry mall hours.
Some plain footways run through mall footprints without indoor tags. They stay routable at all hours.
46 unsheltered edges, 1.8 km, run mostly inside a building footprint with no cover tag.
Those edges carry flag 1024, inside a footprint with cover unverified. They get no shelter flag, and their shade counts as low confidence.
The graph keeps each whole way that has a node in the graph area. Some edges reach 489 m past it.
A road side edge starts half the carriageway width plus 1 m from the road centreline.
The offset shrinks in 0.5 m steps, down to 1.5 m, until no 1 m sample sits inside a ground-level footprint.
559 side edges moved closer to the road. 80 sides still inside a footprint at 1.5 m became 70 centre edges.
Carriageway width comes from the width tag, else lanes x 3.2 m, else the median lane count for that road class.
The class medians are 2 lanes for primary, 2 for secondary and 2 for tertiary roads.
Side offsets run from 1.5 m to 9.0 m, with a median of 4.2 m.
A road tagged with a sidewalk on one side gets one side edge. Roads tagged sidewalk=no or separate keep a centre edge.
Tertiary and larger roads with no sidewalk tag get two side edges without the sidewalk flag.
Both side edges share the road's nodes. Node flags mark crossings, signals, junctions and grade-separated links.
Side edge geometry starts and ends at the offset line, a few metres from its nodes.
The offset ignores real kerb lines. A dual carriageway can get a side edge on its median.
Places snap to the largest routable network within 80 m when possible. 81 places still sit on small islands.
55 named places lie more than 80 m from a routable node, so the app omits them.
Araneta City mall hours come from the operator's page, read on 2026-10-22. The page shows no date of its own.
The Cubao LRT-2 station passage opens at 04:50 and closes at 21:07, the earlier of its two last-train times on the LRTA schedule.
OSM opening hours that the simple parser cannot read are skipped. 0 values were skipped.
Building heights come from OSM height, else OSM levels x 3.74 m, else the Google 2023 median, else a 7.5 m default.
Google fills 59618 OSM building objects with modelled 2023 heights. Google heights stop near 100 m.
1161 OSM building objects over 100 m2 use a 7.5 m default, two levels of 3.74 m. Their shade counts as low confidence.
Each default replaces a Google median under 2.5 m. The default errs low, so a taller real building casts more shade than shown.
3416 OSM building objects of 100 m2 or less have no usable height. Their height is null.
Each building part is its own feature. 5 OSM outlines that parts fully cover are left out.
An outline's Google median uses only the area outside its parts, so a tower does not raise its podium.
Google medians use no presence mask. A mask would change 0.4% of them by more than 5 m.
